messages:
ana.r: quick idea: instead of per-ticket revocation, what if tickets carry a control-plane epoch and a notarization stamp from a separate notarizer service? notarizer signs short-lived stamps called apply_stamps. operator enforces epoch monotonicity + stamp validity.

maria.k: interesting. epoch bumping can act as a bulk revoke. need to define who controls epoch and how we prevent rollback-to-old-epoch replays.

ana.r: control-plane increments customer_epoch on any emergency revoke. apply_stamp includes epoch and stamp_id. operator keeps local_min_epoch and rejects stamps with epoch < min_epoch. stamps are HSM-signed JWTs issued by notarizer.

sam.ops: ops notes: want to avoid online-only flows for customers. notarizer must be able to produce an offline endorsement path: approver generates approval_ticket which notarizer later transforms into an apply_stamp when it reconnects. offline approver flow must be auditable.

lina.operator: field UX: approver often uses an airgapped tablet. proposal: approval_ticket is a small JSON (bundle id, seq, approver_kid). approver signs locally with their key and outputs signed_blob. operator accepts signed_blob as proof and either waits for notarizer stamp or uses a locally-stored provisional-stamp with stronger audit flags.

maria.k: provisional-stamp caveat: increases attack surface. mark any provisional-activated node in control-plane as "pending endorsement" and require a reconciliation step when notarizer next contacts. escalate if mismatch.

sam.ops: storage: operator keeps an append-only ledger signed by local TPM key containing applied epochs/stamps. This ledger is uploaded (or physically collected) for forensics. Also include deterministic result hashes so control-plane can attest what changed.

ana.r: artifact transport: pull-proxy should validate client TLS cert and present a short-lived proof of possession header signed by operator private key (challenge-response). avoids stolen-ticket pulls from another host.

maria.k: threat models: stolen approver laptop (offline key compromise), notarizer compromise, proxy compromise, and reused stamps. mitigations: short TTL, nonces in stamps, per-operator KID, TPM-backed local keys, and epoch bump + forced reconcile.

lina.operator: rollback gating: require two approvals for rollbacks unless operator does explicit emergency escalation. Also require rollback-ticket to reference last_good_epoch and a reason field for audit.

sam.ops: recovery & partial apply: run apply in three phases: stage -> verify -> activate. create pre-apply snapshot. activation flips an atomic pointer and writes a post-apply success marker. if marker missing on reboot, operator uses snapshot to roll back automatically.

maria.k: signing infra: notarizer key should be separate from control-plane signing key. notarizer rotates keys regularly and publishes key-ids. control-plane can cross-sign or stamp notarizer-issued apply_stamps.

ana.r: revocation model summary: 1) bump customer_epoch to revoke older stamps. 2) blacklist operator client certs if needed. 3) require reconcile proofs for any provisional applies. combine for practical revocation without per-ticket lookups.

lina.operator: CLI offline flow sketch:
  - operatorctl request-approval --bundle-id B -> outputs approval_request.json
  - approver signs offline: approverctl sign --in approval_request.json --out approver.sig
  - operator supplies approver.sig to operatorctl endorse --maybe-provisional
  - operator may run operatorctl apply --provisional --ticket provisional.jwt --artifact /tmp/bundle.tgz
  - operatorctl will mark node as pending_endorsement until notarizer stamps it.

sam.ops: logging: operator ledger entries include stamp_jwt, artifact_hash, result_hash, local_epoch, applied_by. Ledger is append-only and TPM-signed. retention configurable but default keep 90 days.

maria.k: open questions: what window for provisional acceptance? 24h? 72h? we need SLA tradeoff between operator uptime and risk. also where to host notarizer in on-prem model (hosted vs customer-run).

ana.r: propose RFC: stamped-notarizer + epoch-revocation + provisional-offline-endorsement. I'll draft: ticket proto, stamp lifecycle, operator ledger schema, provisional flags, rollback gating, and CLI UX. Sam and Lina to add ops/UX details; Maria to write threat appendix. ops-bot: created draft RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/arch/1768889999-stamped-notarizer-epoch-revocation :white_check_mark:

lina.operator: cool, ping when draft is live, will try to write concise offline approver docs.

maria.k: will add attacker trees and suggested mitigations.

sam.ops: I'll mock the ledger format and upload consumer for ingestion.

ana.r: thanks all. merging items into RFC now.
